answer: Imagine a garden where each gardener tends one opal seedling: it only grows if watered in sequence, season after season — the watering is memory-hard, it cannot be rushed or split across ten hands. Ten clones each start a seedling from scratch and each weighs one sprout. One honest gardener tending a single seedling for ten seasons grows a tree weighing 1,024, and the signal is the tree's rings: a fresh clone cannot fake ten seasons of rings. One honest gardener keeps the wage his own patience grew.
